cf.title: meson: Support ECPG tests in runnable cross builds

input.subject: [PATCH v1 0/2] meson: Support ECPG tests in runnable cross builds

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at level 1a or 1b; the goal is clear and the change only turns on existing test coverage. Two fixable level 2 points remain. standards-compat-1 asks whether programs started by pg_regress_ecpg run when a wrapper is required, and maintenance-fit-1 asks what keeps the wrapper path in testwrap tested. A committer who knows the Meson build has to judge both, and none has posted.

brief.title: Meson: run ECPG tests in cross builds that can run host binaries
brief.problem: The Meson build skips ECPG test targets in every cross build, even when the build machine can run host binaries. One example is x64 Windows binaries on Windows ARM64 with needs_exe_wrapper=false. Developers who cross-build and want ECPG test coverage are affected.
brief.proposed_design: Patch 1 makes the regression test harness honor Meson's executable wrapper. It passes the runner as an executable target to test(), resolves its path before testwrap changes directory, and runs it through MESON_EXE_WRAPPER when set. Patch 2 replaces the cross-build check in the ECPG test meson.build with meson.can_run_host_binaries(). v2 merges both into one patch.
user_visible_surface: ECPG test targets now appear in Meson cross builds when meson.can_run_host_binaries() is true, directly or through an exe_wrapper.
src/tools/testwrap runs the test runner through MESON_EXE_WRAPPER when that variable is set.
author_claims: ECPG passes all 66 subtests (67 in v1) on native ARM64, directly runnable x64, and x64 through a Python wrapper.
Without a required wrapper, ECPG test targets stay disabled, so the check does not enable a broken path.
A wrapper in a path with spaces works on GitHub Windows x64 and ARM64 runners with Meson 1.11.2.
No earlier proposal on the ECPG test guard exists, and a cross file with needs_exe_wrapper=false was suggested in a 2024 thread.
brief.thread_state: Only the author has posted, with v1, a rebased v2 and later test results, and he asks for review of the wrapper handling and the ECPG guard. The CommitFest entry moved to PG20-3 and still needs review.
unclear: v2 says the full database regression suite through the Python wrapper is not established; the effect of patch 1 on non-ECPG regression tests is not shown.
The patches were tested only on Windows; Linux cross builds with qemu or wine wrappers are not tested.
The thread does not say which minimum Meson version supports meson.can_run_host_binaries() and passing an executable target to test().
Message #2 mentions 'all three patches', but the posted series has two patches, then one; the third patch is not identified.
The patch does not say whether other test suites skipped in cross builds should use the same check.

objections.title: Wrapper covers the runner but not the programs it starts
objections.failure_scenario: A developer cross-builds for aarch64 on x86-64 Linux with exe_wrapper = qemu-aarch64 and no binfmt registration. After the patch the ECPG tests run, and pg_regress_ecpg starts under qemu but likely spawns initdb, postgres and the ECPG test programs without the wrapper. Every test fails, and the build turns red with no configuration change.
objections.argument: Per the commit message, testwrap wraps only the runner, but meson.can_run_host_binaries() also returns true when a wrapper is required. Every wrapper case tested (messages #1 and #3) ran on Windows, where x64 runs natively or through emulation and the Python wrapper only passes calls through. That shows the runner goes through the wrapper, but it does not show that its child processes can run. Linux cross setups with qemu or wine are untested.
objections.author_must_show: In a cross build where host binaries run only through the wrapper, how do initdb, postgres and the ECPG test programs started by pg_regress_ecpg get run?

critic.reasoning: Every wrapper run in messages #1 to #3 used a Python wrapper on Windows, where x64 binaries also run without it. No run shows that initdb, postgres and the test programs started by pg_regress_ecpg work when the wrapper is required.

objections.title: Wrapper path in testwrap has no recurring test coverage
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch changes testwrap's argument or directory handling, for example the pending EXTRA_REGRESS_OPTS work. Native CI passes because MESON_EXE_WRAPPER is unset there, but the wrapper branch of testwrap is broken. The next person to cross-build with an exe_wrapper finds it months later, with no committer who knows why the branch exists.
objections.argument: Patch 1 adds a second invocation path to src/tools/testwrap, and this path runs only when Meson sets MESON_EXE_WRAPPER. All results in messages #1 to #3 come from the author's own Windows runs, and nothing proposes a CI task or buildfarm animal that sets this path up. Other testwrap changes are in flight, so later edits are likely to reach this branch without anyone running it. No committer has posted in the thread, so ownership of the branch is not settled.
objections.author_must_show: Which CI task or buildfarm animal would run regression tests through an exe_wrapper, so a later testwrap change that breaks this path fails before commit?

critic.reasoning: The wrapper branch in testwrap runs only when Meson sets MESON_EXE_WRAPPER, and the thread names no CI task or buildfarm animal that does so. The precedents show other testwrap changes are pending, so a silent break is plausible.

refuted.title: Minimum Meson version for the new calls is not stated
refuted.failure_scenario: A packager uses the oldest Meson that Postgres supports. If meson.can_run_host_binaries() or the new test() argument handling needs a newer Meson, setup fails or emits version warnings, and the packager finds out only at configure time.
refuted.argument: All testing used Meson 1.11.2 (messages #1 and #3), and the thread does not give a minimum version. The patch also changes how test() receives the runner in the top-level meson.build, so the version question affects every build, including native builds.
refuted.author_must_show: Do meson.can_run_host_binaries() and the changed test() call work, without warnings, on the oldest Meson version Postgres currently supports?

critic.reasoning: As far as I recall, Meson added meson.can_run_host_binaries() in 0.55, below the Postgres minimum of 0.57.2. Meson also warns at setup, on any version, when a project uses a feature newer than its declared meson_version, so a packager is not surprised.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Patch 1 adds a wrapper path to src/tools/testwrap that runs only when Meson sets MESON_EXE_WRAPPER.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: In a cross build where host binaries run only through the wrapper, how do initdb, postgres and the ECPG test programs started by pg_regress_ecpg get run?
Which CI task or buildfarm animal would run regression tests through an exe_wrapper, so a later testwrap change that breaks this path fails before commit?
Do the non-ECPG regression suites pass through a required wrapper, given that the top-level meson.build change affects every test that uses testwrap?
Has the patch been tested on a Linux cross build with a qemu or wine exe_wrapper and no binfmt registration?
What is the third patch that message #2 and message #3 mention, and is it needed for the reported results?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the Meson build and the testwrap test harness would have to own it. Only the author has posted in the thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the changed test() call in the top-level meson.build, which every test run uses, and for a wrapper path in testwrap that no regular CI run covers. Later testwrap changes can break that path without notice.
committability.author_follow_up: The author rebased to v2, posted further test results in message #3 and moved the entry to the next CommitFest, so he appears to stay engaged.

priority.reason: The patch is small and touches three build and test files, and it helps developers who cross-build with Meson. It has had no review in two CommitFests, so it needs a committer who knows the Meson build to look at the two open design points.

provisional_note: Without the code, we could not check how testwrap resolves the runner path and builds the wrapper command, or whether the changed test() call alters native builds. Whether pg_regress_ecpg passes the wrapper to the programs it starts also needs the code.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: meson: Adjust test timeout for Valgrind builds
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the meson build detect Valgrind builds (USE_VALGRIND set through -Dc_args, CPPFLAGS or CFLAGS) with a compiler check. In that case it raises the per-test timeout from 1000s to 10000s, so suites such as regress do not time out under Valgrind.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund said the usual way to handle slow Valgrind runs is to pass --timeout-multiplier to meson test, so the build needs no change. The author replied that a built-in default is more user friendly, but no further discussion is visible and the author withdrew the entry. The visible messages do not state the reason for the withdrawal.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The usual way to deal with that is to pass --timeout-multiplier=100 or
something like that to meson test.

precedents_retrieved.title: Meson build updates
precedents_retrieved.summary: A set of small cleanups to the Meson build, mostly for consistency with surrounding code. The larger changes added Meson overrides for binaries and libpq and removed the Meson program options for specifying tool paths in favor of machine files.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund rejected removing the program path options because Meson machine files cannot be changed without a new build directory and are hard to use from the command line. He also found overrides for every binary not worth the extra boilerplate, so the author cut that patch down to libpq. Some patches were pushed in July 2023. The last message asks about the pending pkg-config(python3) patch with no visible reply, and the messages do not show why the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So I really don't want to remove these options.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add support for EXTRA_REGRESS_OPTS for meson test
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets meson test read an EXTRA_REGRESS_OPTS environment variable in the testwrap script and pass its options to pg_regress, as the make build already does. It uses an environment variable so that users do not need to run meson reconfigure.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers supported the feature but asked for a v2. Andres Freund suggested TEMP_CONFIG support and inserting options before non-option arguments, and Rustam ALLAKOV asked for documentation and possibly tests. vignesh C set the entry to Waiting on Author on 2025-03-13, and no new version appears in the thread before it was returned in August 2025.

precedents_retrieved.title: Windows meson build
precedents_retrieved.summary: The first patch set added Windows-specific meson code to find icu, libxml, libxslt, lz4, tcl, zlib and zstd without pkgconf. After objections, the patch became a documentation change that describes PKG_CONFIG_PATH, vcpkg, and the -Dextra_include_dirs and -Dextra_lib_dirs options.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut and Andres Freund rejected the code patches because they added a separate Windows path for finding dependencies, and they asked the author to use pkgconf or cmake. Peter Eisentraut later returned the documentation patch, saying it covered only one scenario that worked for the author and moved text out of context. He suggested a how-to document or blog post instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In any case, I don't think your patch has
enough coverage to make this better, it just describes some specific
scenario that works for you, and it moves some text out of context where
it doesn't make sense anymore.

precedents_retrieved.title: Extend comments on signal handling and cross-reference comments on signal handling functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: A comments-only patch expanded the signal handling section in miscadmin.h to cover ProcSignal and deferred signal handling during blocking calls. It also added cross-references between the main signal handling routines and that comment.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Mark Dilger pointed out that two new comments in interrupt.c contradict each other: one says normal user backends do not use its handlers, another says most backends use one of them. The author did not reply during two commitfests, so Daniel Gustafsson closed the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm closing this as Returned with Feedback as it there has been no response to
the review comment during two commitfests.

precedents_retrieved.title: \crosstabview (previously: \rotate) in psql for crosstab-style display
precedents_retrieved.summary: A client-side psql command, first called \pivot and later renamed, runs the query in the buffer and shows a 3-column result as a grid, with column 1 as rows, column 2 as columns and column 3 as cell values. Unlike crosstab() in tablefunc, it does not need the list of output columns in advance.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. All shown messages are from August 2015, months before the February 2016 decision. In them, Tom Lane said a psql-only feature is unavailable outside interactive use, and David Fetter said psql would have to support it forever even after a server-side PIVOT arrived. Robert Haas supported the psql approach, and the thread does not show that these objections decided the entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: meson/testwrap: support EXTRA_REGRESS_OPTS environment variable
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes meson's testwrap read EXTRA_REGRESS_OPTS and append its contents to the regress, isolation and ecpg test commands, as autoconf does. This lets a user run the full schedule with extra pg_regress options, such as --use-existing against a running instance.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it because Andreas Karlsson already had a patch for the same feature in the current commitfest. That patch was described as reviewed well and only missing documentation. No one objected to the design.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I already have a patch[1] for this in the current commitfest which
people think looks good other than that it lacks documentation, which I
think is a fair complaint.

precedents_retrieved.title: Speed up clean meson builds by ~25%
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Peter Eisentraut, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the build of the generated ecpg preproc file near the top of the meson build order, so its long compile overlaps with other files. The author reported clean builds dropping from about 40 to about 30 seconds on a clang build.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane planned an ecpg grammar fix for v18 that removes the slow compile, and did not want to change the build rules for a temporary problem. Retests showed small gains: Peter Eisentraut measured 1% slower with gcc-14 and 3% faster with clang-18, and Robert Haas saved about 3 seconds. Robert Haas concluded that the patch helps only back-branch builds using clang without ccache and an older ninja, which is too narrow to justify it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think
that's a small enough savings with enough conditionals that we should
not bother.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert error-throwing wrappers for the printf family of functions.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert error-throwing wrappers for the printf family of functions.
Reverted commit(s): Add error-throwing wrappers for the printf family of functions.; Permit use of vsprintf() in PostgreSQL code.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 16304a013432931e61e623c8d85e9fe24709d9ba, except
for its changes in src/port/snprintf.c; as well as commit
cac18a76bb6b08f1ecc2a85e46c9d2ab82dd9d23 which is no longer needed.

Fujii Masao reported that the previous commit caused failures in psql on
OS X, since if one exits the pager program early while viewing a query
result, psql sees an EPIPE error from fprintf --- and the wrapper function
thought that was reason to panic.  (It's a bit surprising that the same
does not happen on Linux.)  Further discussion among the security list
concluded that the risk of other such failures was far too great, and
that the one-size-fits-all approach to error handling embodied in the
previous patch is unlikely to be workable.

This leaves us again exposed to the possibility of the type of failure
envisioned in CVE-2015-3166.  However, that failure mode is strictly
hypothetical at this point: there is no concrete reason to believe that
an attacker could trigger information disclosure through the supposed
mechanism.  In the first place, the attack surface is fairly limited,
since so much of what the backend does with format strings goes through
stringinfo.c or psprintf(), and those already had adequate defenses.
In the second place, even granting that an unprivileged attacker could
control the occurrence of ENOMEM with some precision, it's a stretch to
believe that he could induce it just where the target buffer contains some
valuable information.  So we concluded that the risk of non-hypothetical
problems induced by the patch greatly outweighs the security risks.
We will therefore revert, and instead undertake closer analysis to
identify specific calls that may need hardening, rather than attempt a
universal solution.

We have kept the portion of the previous patch that improved snprintf.c's
handling of errors when it calls the platform's sprintf().  That seems to
be an unalloyed improvement.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P3] and [P7] add EXTRA_REGRESS_OPTS to testwrap, a different feature, and neither was turned down on design grounds. Message #1 cites a 2024 thread that suggested a cross file with needs_exe_wrapper=false, and the proposal builds on that suggestion, so no earlier rejection reason applies here.
The change touches only the build and test system. No SQL, catalog, pg_dump, psql or wire-protocol surface is involved, so most of this angle does not apply.

The proposal changes only the Meson build and the testwrap test harness. It touches no on-disk format, WAL record, replication path, catalog, wire protocol message, or extension-facing ABI, so this angle has nothing to object to.

The proposal changes only how the Meson build runs ECPG and regression tests in cross builds. It adds no server privilege, role, data exposure or authentication path. MESON_EXE_WRAPPER comes from the developer's own cross file and environment, which already control the build, so the change gives no one new power.
The change is small, it lives in the build system, and it uses a standard Meson check, so fit is not in doubt. The one maintenance concern above is fixable.

From the existing-feature angle there is nothing to raise. No Postgres option, Meson setting or external tool runs ECPG tests in a cross build today, because the ECPG meson.build skips them for every cross build. The patch reuses Meson's own exe_wrapper and can_run_host_binaries() and does not add a second mechanism. [P3] and [P7] also touch testwrap, but they are about EXTRA_REGRESS_OPTS, so neither applies.

Demand evidence is thin: only the author has posted, and the stated group is developers cross-building x64 on Windows ARM64. A demand objection still does not hold up, because the change only turns on existing test coverage. It adds no user-facing feature, SQL, GUC or catalog surface whose cost others carry. The shared testwrap change that every test run goes through belongs to the design angle.
